title: 2018 AMC 12B Problem 20
statement: Let \(ABCDEF\) be a regular hexagon with side length \(1.\) Denote by \(X,\) \(Y,\) and \(Z\) the midpoints of sides \(AB,\) \(CD,\) and \(EF,\) respectively. What is the area of the convex hexagon whose interior is the intersection of the interiors of \(\triangle ACE\) and \(\triangle XYZ?\)

solutions.text:
Place the regular hexagon on the unit circle with \(A=(1,0),\) \(C=(-\tfrac12,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}),\) and \(E=(-\tfrac12,-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}).\) The three specified midpoints are \(X=(\tfrac34,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{4}),\) \(Y=(-\tfrac34,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{4}),\) and \(Z=(0,-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}).\)

Intersecting the side lines of \(\triangle ACE\) and \(\triangle XYZ\) gives the six vertices of their common interior, in cyclic order: \[ \begin{gathered} (-\tfrac12,0),\quad (-\tfrac18,-\tfrac{3\sqrt3}{8}),\\ (\tfrac14,-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{4}),\quad (\tfrac58,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{8}),\\ (\tfrac14,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{4}),\quad (-\tfrac12,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{4}). \end{gathered} \] The shoelace formula applied to these vertices gives area \(\dfrac{15\sqrt3}{32}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
